title: Deep learning segmentation with uncertainty quantification for spinal tuberculosis on fat-suppressed T2-weighted MRI.
summary: In a 50-case external test set, the model achieved Dice 0.858 and pixel-level AUC 0.912; predictive uncertainty correlated with pixel-level error (ρ=0.74). In a nine-physician crossover, uncertainty overlays increased trust ratings and reduced review time. Retrospective 210-patient, three-center study: internal five-fold cross-validation and a separate 50-case external test set, plus a nine-physician within-subject crossover. Clinical decision-support measures do not establish better treatment or patient outcomes.
ai_technology: Improved nnU-Net combines boundary-aware loss with Monte Carlo dropout to segment spinal tuberculosis lesions and estimate pixel-level uncertainty on fat-suppressed T2 MRI.
organization: Department of Orthopedics, General Hospital of Ningxia Medical University, Yinchuan, Ningxia, China

source_review.scope: The publisher full text reports an uncertainty-guided nnU-Net segmentation of spinal tuberculosis lesions on FS-T2 MRI in 210 patients from three centers. On a 50-case external test set, Dice was 0.858 and pixel-level AUC 0.912; uncertainty tracked segmentation error (Spearman ρ=0.74), and a nine-physician within-subject study found higher trust scores and shorter review time with uncertainty overlays. The first located result-bearing version is the publisher article dated 2026-07-29; exact-title/DOI searches did not locate an earlier matching repository version, without asserting global priority. The retrospective test cohort and small reader study support a bounded segmentation/decision-support result, not improved patient outcomes.
